newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak rates fall sharply, seen back above 20pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovak rates fall sharply, seen back above 20pct.

text.p: Slovak interbank rates fell sharply on Thursday but dealers said the decline was only a short-term move at the end of the minimum reserves requirement (PMR) period.

One-day funds, still the most traded maturity on the Slovak money market, fell to around 11 percent after opening at some 25 percent. But traders expected the rates to climb back to above 20 percent in coming days.
"This (decline) happens at the end of each PMR period. I expect the next period to start (on Friday) with rates at 25 to 26 percent," said Jaroslav Hora, chief trader at VUB Bank.

Dealers said the banking sector would probably meet its PMR on Thursday but further developments were under the central bank's (NBS) control. They predicted no substantial liquidity inflows from the NBS in the near future.

The central bank at present monitors money market liquidity on a daily basis and influences this through its repo tenders. It now has some 10.5 billion crown in the interbank market extended through its repos.

"So far all repos offered up to one week money which leaves the NBS an easy way to squeeze the market within a short time. The sector really lacks any longer funds...such money is just not here and it seems it will not come soon," Hora said.

The NBS on Thursday sold unspecified tranches of six-day and 70-day treasury bills from its portfolio to drain crowns from the market, which, dealers said, showed it was fully aware of the market liquidity flows.

"The central bank knew some three billion crowns were to come to the market from maturing T-bills and it wanted to shorten the sector to get it closer to 100 percent of PMR fulfilment," said Rastislav Zivor of ING Bank.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector as of July 30 fulfilled its minimum reserve requirements at 100 percent.
The daily volume of minimum reserves for commercial banks totals 36.583 billion crowns in the current reserves period ending July 31.
